channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Italy favours compromise in railway company probe
item.description: Italy’s Competition Authority is likely to accept commitments from the country’s national railway infrastructure manager to close an exclusionary abuse of dominance probe, a senior agency official has said.

item.title: Cœuré: EU handling of ATT probes would have been “more straightforward”
item.description: It would have been simpler for the European Commission to take the lead in probing Apple’s App Tracking Transparency framework instead of having five national antitrust enforcers progress separate investigations, according to the head of France’s Competition Authority.

item.title: CMA assisting Ministry of Defence in red tape review
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority is helping the Ministry of Defence to identify potentially anticompetitive regulations governing autonomous weapons and technologies.

item.title: Italy open to handing WhatsApp investigation to EU
item.description: Italy’s Competition Authority is “happy” to drop its abuse of dominance investigation into WhatsApp should the European Commission extend the scope of its own probe.

item.title: CMA not “going soft on enforcement”, Cardell says
item.description: Working in a “policy-informed way” should not be confused with succumbing to “improper political influence”, the chief executive of the UK's Competition and Markets Authority has said.

item.title: Portugal plotting Nvidia probe
item.description: Portugal’s Competition Authority is in discussions with the European Commission about launching an investigation into Nvidia.

item.title: Coal front: The Tipline for 26 February 2026
item.description: Vanguard is the first asset manager to settle Texas-led claims of an anti-coal conspiracy. “Coal is an essential industry to support America’s ever-growing energy demands, and my office will continue to uproot and destroy any attempt by investment giants to push a woke agenda that puts American energy at risk,” said Texas attorney general Ken Paxton in a statement on Thursday. item.title: Wall Street accused of using Kirkland to “punish” Optimum
item.description: Asset managers including JPMorgan, Apollo Global Management and BlackRock “bullied” Kirkland & Ellis into dropping Optimum as a client, the telecommunications company has alleged.

item.title: Netflix walks away from Warner Bros deal
item.description: Netflix has abandoned its pursuit of Warner Bros hours after Paramount submitted a superior offer.

item.title: Ferguson: "No political antitrust problem at FTC”
item.description: Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson has rejected claims that antitrust enforcement has become overtly political during his tenure, stating those concerns have been “mostly generated by the press”.
